briefings.title: Claude Code Head Boris Cherny: Insane Growth, Tokenmaxxing, AI Agents' Next Frontier
briefings.tldr: Anthropic’s Claude Code and co-work agentic products are experiencing explosive, exponential growth, shifting AI from basic conversational chatbots to autonomous agents that can control computers and use APIs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Anthropic’s Claude Code and co-work agentic products are experiencing explosive, exponential growth, shifting AI from basic conversational chatbots to autonomous agents that can control computers and use APIs. This shift has enabled immense productivity gains, with Anthropic engineers writing 250% more code, even as the company scales its infrastructure to meet unprecedented demand.

---

## Unprecedented Hypergrowth and Self-Generating Code

* **Exponential Growth Metrics:** Anthropic is experiencing massive scaling, with CEO Dario Amodei previously reporting an 80x year-over-year increase in demand. 
    * While Anthropic’s ARR was at $4 billion last year, host Alex Kantrowitz noted that current market rumors suggest ARR has skyrocketed toward $45 billion.
    * Cherny stated that since the release of Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 in May of last year, followed by updates 4.5, 4.6, and 4.7, product growth has inflected repeatedly at a pace unlike anything he has witnessed in his tech career.
* **Coding Productivity Gains:** The volume of code written per engineer at Anthropic has increased by approximately 250% since the introduction of Claude Code, with code quality and system reliability remaining entirely stable.
* **Self-Building AI:** In a remarkable recursive feedback loop, Claude Code and its sister product co-work are now 100% written by Claude Code.
* **Widespread Adoption:** At a recent Y Combinator talk, Cherny asked a room of several hundred founders how many write 100% of their software using Claude Code; nearly half of the room raised their hands.

## The Shift from Chatbots to Tool-Using Agents

* **The Agent Paradigm:** Unlike early-generation chatbots, Claude Code and co-work operate as autonomous agents. They do not just predict text; they use computer tools, browse the web, edit local files, and hook into external APIs (such as QuickBooks for small business bookkeeping).
    * Cherny highlighted a personal use case where co-work navigated his email and calendar, caught scheduling mistakes, and autonomously booked eight flights and five hotels across a complex five-city itinerary.
* **The Rise of Parallel Workflows:** Power users are no longer running just one Claude instance at a time. Cherny noted that he routinely runs five instances simultaneously during the day, and up to hundreds or thousands of Claudes in parallel overnight to execute complex tasks.
* **Auto Mode and Safety:** To combat prompt fatigue—where users blindly click "approve" on safety dialogs—Anthropic introduced "Auto Mode." 
    * **Autonomous Safety Routing:** Instead of asking the user for permission for every individual action, Claude asks a secondary Claude instance if a tool call is safe to make, utilizing thousands of background benchmarks. Tests show this secondary-agent validation is actually safer than manual human approval.

## Addressing "Tokenmaxxing" and Infrastructure Constraints

* **The Tokenmaxxing Phenomenon:** Reports have emerged of employees at major tech firms (like Amazon) purposefully running useless, hours-long automated AI loops to artificially boost their internal AI usage metrics to meet corporate mandates.
    * **Cherny's Perspective:** Cherny does not believe tokenmaxxing represents a significant share of overall demand. He advises companies to offer "psychological safety" and free token allotments to encourage organic workflow experimentation rather than gamifying usage through leaderboards.
* **The "90s PC" Productivity Parallel:** Cherny compared the current AI transition to the 1990s adoption of personal computers. Companies back then bought PCs but saw no productivity gains until they threw out their physical filing cabinets and redesigned their entire business processes around the computer. AI requires the same structural reorganization.
* **Resolving Rate Limits:** Heavy users often complain of hitting strict rate limits. To resolve this, Anthropic has doubled its 5-hour rate limits, increased weekly limits, and onboarded massive new server capacity via Elon Musk’s "Colossus" supercomputer cluster.

## Redefining Business Moats and the "World Model" Debate

* **Declining vs. Growing Moats:** Evaluating AI's impact on software through the "Seven Powers" framework, Cherny predicts a shift in corporate defensibility:
    * **Switching Costs Will Decrease:** AI agents make it incredibly easy to port data and switch from vendor A to vendor B, eroding traditional software lock-in.
    * **Network Effects and Economies of Scale Will Strengthen:** Structural moats like proprietary user networks and physical manufacturing scale (e.g., TSMC or massive cloud infrastructure) will become even more valuable.
* **The World Model Debate:** Meta’s Yann LeCun has argued that LLMs cannot make reliable agents because they lack a "world model" and cannot predict the consequences of their actions.
    * **Cherny's Counter-Argument:** Cherny strongly disagrees with LeCun's skepticism, pointing to Claude's surprising ability to plan, reason, and look ahead (such as planning the second line of a poem while generating the first). Cherny issued an open invitation for LeCun to sit down and use Claude Code for an hour to see its planning capabilities firsthand.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "Claude Code is 100% written by Claude Code. Co-work is 100% written by Claude Code. An increasing number of features are fully written by Claude Code across Anthropic and products." — **Boris Cherny**

> "I don't write code. I prompt Claude. And actually nowadays, mostly what I'm doing is I have a Claude that prompts other Claudes. So I don't even talk to Claude. I have a Claude that's talking to my Claudes." — **Boris Cherny**

> "The amount of code written per engineer at Anthropic has grown something like 250% since we introduced Claude Code... and this is while keeping code quality and revivability and all these things stable." — **Boris Cherny**

> "I would put out an offer to Yann [LeCun], if he wants to sit down and Claude Code together for an hour, I'd love to show him. And then I'm curious to hear what he thinks." — **Boris Cherny**

briefings.title: Gavin Baker on Orbital Compute, TSMC, and Frontier Models
briefings.tldr: The artificial intelligence expansion represents the most extraordinary acceleration of revenue and compute demand in the history of capitalism, driven by unprecedented inflections like Anthropic’s massive ARR growth.
briefings.summary_markdown:
1. **TL;DR**  
The artificial intelligence expansion represents the most extraordinary acceleration of revenue and compute demand in the history of capitalism, driven by unprecedented inflections like Anthropic’s massive ARR growth. However, sustaining this trajectory requires overcoming physical constraints in energy ("watts") and silicon manufacturing ("wafers"), forcing a shift toward custom silicon, usage-based enterprise pricing, and highly advanced orbital compute networks.

---

## The Unprecedented Scale of AI Growth & Valuation Dynamics

* **The Anthropic Milestone:** Anthropic added approximately $11 billion in ARR in an incredibly short period. To put this in perspective, it took three of the most successful SaaS companies of the last decade—Palantir, Snowflake, and Databricks—ten years of collective operations and tens of thousands of employees to build businesses of that combined scale.
* **Disparities in Capital Efficiency:** Anthropic has operated with roughly 80% less capital burn than OpenAI to reach a comparable revenue scale. Consequently, Anthropic is positioned to potentially generate positive cash flow this year, demonstrating a significantly higher structural return on invested capital (ROIC).
* **The Transition to Usage-Based Pricing:** AI is rapidly shifting from "all-you-can-eat" flat-rate subscriptions to pay-by-the-drink usage pricing. 
    * This shift mirrors the cellular telecom expansion of 2005–2007, where usage-based pricing unlocked massive, compounding revenue curves. 
    * Unconstrained by flat-rate boundaries, top-tier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are positioned to easily clear $200 billion in ARR.
* **Cross-Sectional Valuation Anomalies:** Public market valuations currently exhibit massive logical contradictions. Semiconductor capital equipment companies trade at 40x next-quarter annualized earnings, while DRAM (memory) manufacturers trade at mid-single-digit multiples, despite the vertical pricing growth of High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM).

---

## Solving the Compute Bottleneck: Watts and Wafers

* **The "Watts" Bottleneck & Zoning:** Near-term energy availability is constrained more by zoning, approvals, and turbine casting limits than by grid capacity. However, capitalism is rapidly adapting, with massive capital expenditure projects coming online to expand grid infrastructure and repurpose alternative energy sources by 2027–2028.
* **The Case for Orbital Compute:** Long-term energy limitations will inevitably be resolved by migrating inference compute into space.
    * **Racks in Space:** Orbital compute is not characterized by giant, floating space stations, but by standard server racks (such as a 3,000-pound Nvidia Blackwell rack) operating as individual satellites in sun-synchronous orbits.
    * **Thermal and Power Efficiency:** In sun-synchronous orbits, 500-foot-long solar panels remain constantly illuminated, while massive radiators extend into perpetual shade. 
    * **Inter-Rack Connectivity:** Racks are linked into virtual data centers using vacuum-traveling lasers, building upon the laser-communication architectures SpaceX already deploys at scale on Starlink V3 satellites.
* **TSMC as a Bubble Preventer:** Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) single-handedly prevents a speculative hyper-bubble by strictly limiting wafer supply. If TSMC expanded capacity to meet unconstrained demand, Nvidia could potentially sell $2 trillion to $3 trillion in GPUs by 2026/2027, leading to a catastrophic overbuild.
* **The Texas "TeraFab" Initiative:** A joint venture involving Elon Musk, Tesla, and SpaceX aims to build the world’s largest fabrication facility in America. Partnering with Intel to access 50 years of institutional manufacturing knowledge, the project leverages Musk's ability to construct hardware facilities in a fraction of standard timelines (such as building the Memphis supercluster in 122 days).

---

## The Chip Design Battlefield: Prefill, Decode, and Hardware Lifespans

* **The Iron Triangle of Chip Design:** Similar to military tank design (balancing attack, defense, and mobility), chip architects must negotiate rigid physical trade-offs between memory capacity, memory bandwidth, and compute power within TSMC's manufacturing rules.
* **Prefill vs. Decode Disaggregation:** Modern model architectures allow designers to optimize chips by separating these two distinct phases:
    * **Prefill (Loading the Cannon):** The process of ingest-loading the prompt and context, which is heavily memory-capacity bound.
    * **Decode (Firing the Cannon):** The step-by-step generation of output tokens, which is memory-bandwidth constrained.
* **Cerebras and Wafer-Scale Computing:** Chip startups cannot succeed by trying to build a "better GPU" because Nvidia maintains insurmountable scale and supply chain advantages. Startups must do something fundamentally different and physically difficult. Cerebras achieved this through wafer-scale engine architecture, keeping massive compute and memory on a single giant silicon wafer to bypass traditional chip-to-chip packaging bottlenecks.
* **Salvaging GPU Capital and Private Credit:** The disaggregation of prefill and inference tasks allows older GPUs (like Nvidia Hopper or Ampere architectures) to remain highly productive. By placing ultra-fast inference processors (like Cerebras or Grok LPUs) in front of older GPUs to handle prefill, operators can extend the useful life of legacy silicon to 10–15 years, securing the underlying assets of the massive GPU private credit market.

---

## The Application Layer Crisis and Geopolitical Realities

* **Trillions in Value Destroyed:** At the application layer, AI has actually net-destroyed trillions of dollars of enterprise software value. Shallow SaaS applications have struggled to adapt as foundational frontier models commoditize basic software workflows, though highly specialized coding tools (such as Cursor and Cognition) remain strong exceptions.
* **The New Prisoner's Dilemma of Frontier Labs:** Model builders face a critical strategic choice: do they release their state-of-the-art weights via open APIs, or keep them entirely closed? 
    * Releasing them open-source allows competitors—particularly resource-constrained Chinese firms—to rapidly "distill" and clone the models using cheap reasoning traces.
    * If the top Western labs collectively agree to stop releasing frontier APIs, they can effectively halt the rapid catch-up of open-source competitors.
* **Geopolitical and Battlefield AI Dominance:** The war in Ukraine has demonstrated that battlefield superiority is no longer governed solely by physical hardware or drone counts, but by the sophistication of real-time targeting and orchestration AI. This algorithmic edge is shifting the global balance of power, potentially ushering in a new era of Pax Americana driven by Western computational dominance.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "Anthropic added their combined businesses in one month. It's... nothing like that has ever happened in the history of capitalism. Forget my career, just the flat out history of capitalism, the history of business. It's wild."  
> — **Gavin Baker**

> "If Taiwan Semi did what Jensen wanted, I think Nvidia could sell $2 trillion of GPUs in '26 or '27... but there is a limit where consumers would consume so much that you probably would be in an overbuild. And so Taiwan Semi, if we don't get a bubble, like we need to throw a party for them because they will have single-handedly prevented a bubble."  
> — **Gavin Baker**

> "The machine gun is here, and if we do not all become masters of the machine gun, we're going to get mastered. So I am trying to become a master of the machine gun, and then, you know, I'm optimistic there's a long period of time where... you will have advantages using the machine gun."  
> — **Gavin Baker**

briefings.title: Global Keynote: The Beginning of Better | SAP Sapphire Madrid 2026
briefings.tldr: SAP Sapphire Madrid 2026 marks SAP's pivot from a traditional enterprise software provider to a Business AI company.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
SAP Sapphire Madrid 2026 marks SAP's pivot from a traditional enterprise software provider to a Business AI company. By merging its 50-year ERP database with generative AI, SAP has launched the Business AI Platform and the Autonomous Suite, deploying 224 specialized agents and 51 assistants designed to execute mission-critical business processes with 100% accuracy.

---

## The SAP Business AI Platform: Build, Reason, and Govern

To move beyond the limitations of public LLMs—which lack corporate context and data privacy frameworks—SAP has introduced the **Business AI Platform** to serve as the technological backbone of the autonomous enterprise.

* **The Rich Context Layer:** Infuses generative AI with the internal "brain" of the ERP, mapping processes across over 7 million data fields using a custom Knowledge Graph.
    * **SAP Domain Models:** Trained directly on SAP’s proprietary code to interpret complex, customer-specific business rules.
* **Joule Studio 2.0:** An open, agnostic development environment that lets users build multi-agent workflows using SAP or third-party LLMs.
    * **Developer Incentives:** SAP is offering Joule Studio 2.0 and its runtime environment free of charge until the end of 2026, alongside a €100 million investment to accelerate partner ecosystem development.
    * **n8n Workflow Integration:** Workflow automation platform n8n is deeply integrated into Joule Studio 2.0, allowing users to connect SAP data to hundreds of external, non-SAP systems without writing code.
* **Unified Business Data Cloud (BDC):** Acts as a semantic data fabric across multi-cloud environments.
    * **Strategic Acquisitions:** SAP announced its intention to acquire **Dremio** (a high-performance, federated data lakehouse supporting open formats like Apache Iceberg) and **Prior Labs** (a frontier AI lab for tabular foundation models like TabPFN).
    * **Tabular Foundation Models:** The new **SAP-RPT-1.5** model offers high-accuracy tabular predictions and a Chat API for real-time "what-if" simulations and predictive business forecasting.
* **Enterprise-Grade Governance:** Built directly on **SAP LeanIX**, the new **AI Agent Hub** (launching Q3 2026) acts as a central command center to catalog, monitor, and manage the compliance of SAP and non-SAP agents.

---

## The Autonomous Suite and Joule Work

SAP is transforming its legacy systems of execution into an **Autonomous Suite** spanning five core functional domains: Finance, Spend, Supply Chain, Human Capital Management (HCM), and Customer Experience (CX).

* **Multi-Agent Orchestration:** Launching with **224 out-of-the-box agents** and **51 assistants** that coordinate autonomously to complete fragmented enterprise tasks.
* **Joule Work & "Spaces":** Replaces traditional transactional screens with an "app-less" zero-UI experience. Context-driven, transactional, and analytical screens dynamically generate on-the-fly to facilitate human-in-the-loop approvals.
* **Company Memory:** Built on SAP Signavio, this context graph captures unstructured "tribal knowledge" (PDFs, Teams messages, emails, process models) and refines them into "process atoms" that instruct agents on corporate policies and historical exception-handling.
* **Audit-Ready Compliance:** Developed in coordination with external auditing firms, SAP’s finance-focused agents operate under a SOX-compliant, ISO-certified framework to guarantee trace-level auditability.
* **Hybrid Support via RISE:** For enterprises mid-migration, SAP is enabling a significant portion of Joule Assistants to run on hybrid landscapes, including S/4HANA on-premise and legacy ECC environments.

---

## Industry AI and Real-World Value Realization

SAP is deploying tailored Industry AI solutions across 26 sectors to deliver concrete business outcomes rather than disjointed software packages.

* **Deloitte Partnership:** Deloitte has built 78+ industry-specific agents on SAP's platform. Internally, thousands of Deloitte consultants use *Joule for Consultants*, realizing up to a 30% reduction in time spent on daily tasks.
* **H&M Group Digital Transformation:** Leveraging RISE with SAP, BDC, and SuccessFactors, H&M co-developed:
    * **Store Intelligence Agent:** Scans real-time market signals (e.g., local events, localized demand surges) to proactively recommend next-best-actions, trending apparel features, and store floor configurations.
    * **Store Concierge Agent:** Blends online and in-store customer experiences to deliver real-time stock availability and highly personalized outfit recommendations.
* **Automated Asset Management (RWE):** Multi-agent processes diagnose turbine defects, prep technician dispatch, and deliver real-time onsite manuals, aiming to decrease unplanned wind-farm downtime by 15%.
* **Revenue Growth Management (Coca-Cola HBC):** Automates complex settlement reconciliation processes across 29 countries, auto-resolving standard distribution exceptions and surfacing root-cause analyses for disputes.

---

## Strategic Sovereignty and Technology Alliances

To serve regulated industries, SAP is emphasizing absolute security boundaries and regional data compliance.

* **Mistral AI and Cohere Partnerships:** 
    * The **Mistral AI** platform (featuring Le Chat and AI Studio) and **Cohere North** are now generally available on SAP Cloud Infrastructure within sovereign European data centers, offering a 100% European-hosted AI stack.
* **Nvidia OpenShell Integration:** SAP is integrating Nvidia's open-source **OpenShell** framework to secure enterprise AI at scale. OpenShell guarantees that agents operate strictly within permitted data boundaries, use authorized tools, and generate fully traceable execution paths.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "If agents run your payroll, your financial close, do your demand and supply chain planning, 80% accuracy is just not good enough. When you run the world's most mission-critical business processes, your agents should not guess."  
> — *Christian Klein, CEO of SAP*

> "Soon every company will have a workforce of agents. These specialized agents will not replace enterprise software. They will make enterprise software more powerful than ever."  
> — *Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia*

> "By partnering together, we are bringing world-class European-built models... and SAP is bringing what no one else can do: deep business context. The processes, the data, the workflows that are actually running the companies."  
> — *Arthur Mensch, CEO of Mistral AI*

> "Great software adapts to the person, not just the task."  
> — *Sebastian Steinhaeuser, Chief Operating Officer of SAP*

briefings.title: Palmer Luckey Wants America to Win
briefings.tldr: To counter growing global threats, the United States must transition from "world police" to a "world gun store" by arming allies with cheap, autonomous, and rapidly deployable defense systems.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
To counter growing global threats, the United States must transition from "world police" to a "world gun store" by arming allies with cheap, autonomous, and rapidly deployable defense systems. To outpace China, America must abandon bloated, slow "cost-plus" defense contracting, aggressively reclaim its physical manufacturing base, and reform a patent system that currently serves as a blueprint for foreign adversaries.

***

## From "World Police" to "World Gun Store"
* **A Shift in Strategic Doctrine:** The US no longer possesses the domestic political will to sustain long, multi-trillion-dollar "boots-on-the-ground" foreign wars. Instead of acting as global police, the US must act as a supplier.
    * **Equipping Willing Allies:** The US should focus on arming nations that are willing to fight for themselves (e.g., Japan, Taiwan, Germany) rather than sending American troops to defend nations that lack the domestic will to self-defend.
* **Competing as a Global Supplier:** To function effectively as the "world's gun store," the US military-industrial complex must operate like a competitive commercial enterprise.
    * This requires keeping inventory in stock, meeting delivery deadlines, and recognizing that sovereign buyers have alternative purchasing options in Russia and China.

## Defense Products vs. Cost-Plus Contracting
* **The "Cost-Plus" Incentive Trap:** Traditional defense "primes" (e.g., Lockheed Martin, RTX, Boeing) rely heavily on government-funded "cost-plus" contracts, which financially reward companies for delays, inefficiencies, and budget overruns.
* **The "Defense Product" Model:** Anduril operates as a defense *product* company rather than a traditional contractor. 
    * **Private R&D Investment:** Anduril uses its own capital to develop products and reinvests 100% of its revenue back into internal research and development. 
    * **High Margins on Cheaper Hardware:** By producing hardware that is faster and significantly cheaper to manufacture, Anduril achieves up to a 40% profit margin on mature products while selling them to the government for a fraction of the competitors' cost.
* **Case Study: The YFQ-44 Fury:** Anduril invested $900 million of its own money to develop the US Air Force's first autonomous fighter jet, beating out traditional aerospace giants.
    * The aircraft progressed from contract signing to its first flight in just 556 days—making it the fastest clean-sheet jet fighter development program in modern history.
* **Limits of the Product Model:** Private speculation cannot fund every defense asset. Extremely high-cost capital projects (such as nuclear aircraft carriers or bioweapon defense research) still require direct government backing and oversight.

## The China Challenge and Hollowed-Out US Manufacturing
* **Unbalanced Purchasing Power:** While the US defense budget sits around $900 billion compared to China’s estimated $400–$500 billion, China achieves up to a 10x return on every dollar spent due to domestic supply chains and highly automated manufacturing.
* **The Loss of Real Engineering:** The US has decoupled innovation from physical manufacturing, turning American engineers into "architecture astronauts" who layout high-level designs but rely on Chinese engineers to solve actual manufacturing, electrical, and mechanical problems. 
    * **Raw Materials and Supply Chains:** True technological sovereignty requires control over raw feedstocks. Relying on China for critical tech hardware component production undermines US national security.
* **Unified Military Purpose:** China has structured its military with a single, highly focused objective: invading and occupying Taiwan. By contrast, the US military must build and maintain a force capable of fighting across 2 to 2.5 diverse global fronts simultaneously.

## Patent Reform, Capital Markets, and AI Warfare
* **Patents as Adversarial Blueprints:** The current Western patent database acts as an open-source instruction manual for China. Because patents require public disclosure, foreign adversaries can immediately copy technologies while Western competitors must wait 20 years for patent expiration.
    * **National Security Patents:** Luckey advocates for a massive expansion of "classified patents"—allowing companies (like Google in the field of AI) to secure intellectual property rights without disclosing highly sensitive technical details to the global public.
* **US Capital Markets as a Strategic Weapon:** Unlike the highly centralized, state-subsidized Chinese tech sector, US venture capital operates as a vital playground for high-risk, rapid innovation. 
* **Demystifying AI on the Battlefield:** AI used for military targeting and piloting is highly deterministic, verifiable, and rule-bound—unlike conversational "large language models" (LLMs) that hallucinate. Military AI is designed to reliably identify specific, un-ignorable signatures (e.g., distinguishing a Chinese destroyer from a fishing boat).

## Silicon Valley's Cultural Split and Anduril's Patriotism
* **The Tech-Military Divorce:** A distinct cultural rift emerged in Silicon Valley in the early 2010s, with multinational tech workers frequently protesting military projects (such as Google employees forcing the company to cancel Pentagon contracts). 
    * Major tech companies often brand themselves as "transnational" entities rather than American companies, partly for overseas tax sheltering and partly due to a globalist corporate culture.
* **Anduril's Counter-Culture:** 
    * **Veteran Integration:** Service veterans make up 15% to 20% of Anduril’s 7,000-person workforce, anchoring the company’s product designs in real-world operational needs.
    * **Forward Deployments:** Unlike companies that keep staff remote, Anduril routinely sends engineers directly to active conflict zones (including Ukraine and the Middle East) to iterate on hardware features in the field alongside combat operators.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "The United States has a history of fighting for other countries that maybe aren't very interested in fighting for themselves... It doesn't make sense for us to send our people to go die for a country or a form of government or anything that's not directly aligned with US interest if they're not willing to die for themselves." — **Palmer Luckey**

> "We're not teaching engineers how to be engineers anymore. We're not teaching designers how to actually design things to be manufactured; we're teaching them how to be high-level design shops that put together design packages that get sent to the real engineers in China and they actually figure out how to do the work." — **Palmer Luckey**

> "Patents are Chinese instruction manuals... Western companies patent things so that they can trade temporary exclusivity on an idea in exchange for eventually it enters the public domain. And all that really means, in practice, is that... China can just rip it off right away and Western companies can only rip it off after 20 years." — **Palmer Luckey**

briefings.title: Pfizer CEO: How AI Will Reshape the Future of Medicine | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Under CEO Albert Bourla, Pfizer is pivoting post-pandemic by investing heavily in oncology and obesity therapeutics, driving organizational agility through decentralized AI, and adapting to compete with China’s rapidly accelerating, low-cost biotech ecosystem.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Under CEO Albert Bourla, Pfizer is pivoting post-pandemic by investing heavily in oncology and obesity therapeutics, driving organizational agility through decentralized AI, and adapting to compete with China’s rapidly accelerating, low-cost biotech ecosystem.

---

## Post-COVID Pivot and Strategic Acquisitions

*   **Portfolio Rationalization:** Pfizer deliberately divested its consumer healthcare and off-patent generic divisions to focus strictly on high-risk, high-reward innovative medicine.
    *   Albert Bourla (Chairman and CEO of Pfizer) emphasizes that a corporation's role is to excel at a few things, whereas hedging is the role of the investor.
*   **The Post-Pandemic Financial Cliff:** Pfizer experienced a massive revenue drop from its COVID-19 portfolio, falling from $56 billion in 2022 to just $6 billion in 2023. This drop challenged internal confidence but validated the company's focus on long-term resilience.
*   **The Seagen Acquisition ($43 Billion+):** Pfizer acquired Seagen to gain a dominant position in Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs), a highly promising class of cancer drugs.
    *   **ADC Precision Technology:** Bourla compares ADCs to "extremely precise missiles" where an antibody acts as a biological GPS to target cancer cells, and the payload (the drug) acts as a warhead, sparing healthy tissue.
*   **The Metsera Acquisition (Obesity Portfolio):** Following scientific setbacks that forced the cancellation of internal assets due to liver toxicity, Pfizer acquired Metsera to secure a competitive foothold in the obesity space.
    *   **Competitive Outlook:** Phase 2 clinical data confirmed Metsera's potential to deliver a monthly dosing regimen, which would offer a major advantage over the weekly products currently marketed by Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk.

## Optimizing R&D and Clinical Success Rates

*   **Outperforming Industry Success Rates:** Pfizer's clinical success rate is 18–19%, nearly double the pharmaceutical industry average of 10%.
    *   **Improved R&D Metrics:** Under restructured governance, Phase 2 clinical success rates jumped from under 20% to over 50%, and regulatory approval rates now sit near 95%.
*   **Eliminating Operational Silos:** To fix past issues where Pfizer successfully developed molecules but miscalculated their commercial viability, Bourla unified early-stage discovery and late-stage development under a single end-to-end R&D leader.
*   **A Culture of Organizational Confidence:** To build self-confidence within a changing organization, Bourla actively highlights and scales up localized successes rather than letting the corporate focus dwell solely on failures.

## The AI Revolution and Decentralized Transformation

*   **The Five-Year Impact:** While Bourla is skeptical of claims that AI will cure all diseases in 15 years, he expects AI to fundamentally reshape the standard of care, drug target discovery, and manufacturing by 2030.
*   **Machine Learning in Practice:** Pfizer's COVID-19 antiviral pill, Paxlovid, was one of the first highly impactful global molecules discovered using machine learning.
*   **Decentralized AI Governance:** Pfizer rejected a centralized AI model in favor of giving decentralized business units (manufacturing, research, commercial) direct accountability and resources to build their own AI use cases.
*   **Fostering AI Literacy:** To overcome employee fear of displacement, Pfizer launched voluntary training programs for thousands of workers and is implementing internal AI fluency certifications.

## Geopolitical Competition: China’s Rise in Biotech

*   **Scientific Dominance:** In the 2025 Nature Index rankings for scientific output, eight of the top ten global universities were Chinese, with Harvard being the sole US institution in the top ten.
*   **China’s Biotech Infrastructure:** Through meticulous five-year planning, China has built a competent regulatory body modeled on the US FDA, established strong intellectual property (IP) protection, and created a fast-track judiciary system to resolve patent disputes.
*   **The Competitiveness Gap:** Chinese biotech firms operate at half the cost and three times the speed of Western pharma giants. Bourla warns that Western companies have a five-year window to transform through technology before China begins scaling its own drugs globally.
*   **Western Policy Recommendation:** Bourla advises Western governments to stop spending 80% of their energy trying to slow China down, which he views as a waste of resources. Instead, they must focus 80% of their efforts on improving domestic R&D speed, university funding, and regulatory efficiency.

## Leadership, Corporate Culture, and Personal Heritage

*   **Culture Over Strategy:** Bourla believes that culture is more important than leadership and strategy because a strong culture elevates the performance of all employees, turning average performers into high achievers.
*   **360-Degree Feedback System:** In 2019, Pfizer implemented a biannual evaluation system where supervisors are rated entirely by their peers and direct reports on decisiveness, vision, and communication.
*   **Managing Executive Influence:** Recognizing that his passionate Mediterranean style can occasionally stifle open debate, Bourla uses structured "rounds" in meetings to ensure all executives speak before he shares his own conclusions.
*   **Personal Heritage of Resilience:** Bourla credits his unrelenting optimism to his mother, a Holocaust survivor who narrowly escaped a firing squad in Greece. Her survival instilled in him a lifelong belief that "nothing is impossible" and a focus on opportunities over setbacks.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "I’m a believer that a corporation's role is not to hedge. It is to be very good at a few things. Investors' role is to hedge." 
> — Albert Bourla, Chairman and CEO of Pfizer

> "No one follows a pessimist... Pessimists are usually right. But there is nothing great that has happened in humanity without an optimist behind it. Nothing."
> — Albert Bourla, Chairman and CEO of Pfizer

> "[The US] should stop trying, with all the heart and brains that they have, to put 80% of their effort into how to slow down China. Very big mistake... We should put 80% of our focus and effort into how to become better than China." 
> — Albert Bourla, Chairman and CEO of Pfizer

briefings.title: Silicon Valley’s Case Against The Wealth Tax
briefings.tldr: The proposed billionaire wealth tax is a politically motivated "asset seizure" that is highly impractical to enforce and risks driving critical tax revenue and jobs out of high-tax states.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
The proposed billionaire wealth tax is a politically motivated "asset seizure" that is highly impractical to enforce and risks driving critical tax revenue and jobs out of high-tax states. Instead of vilifying the wealthy, policymakers should focus on structural solutions such as closing margin loan loopholes, deregulating high-cost sectors like healthcare and housing, and enacting voting reforms to empower the moderate majority.

---

## The Core Arguments Against the Proposed Wealth Tax

The proposed 2026 Billionaire Tax Act in California (a one-time 5% tax on assets of $1 billion or more) and its federal counterpart face severe pushback from prominent tech investors and political strategists who argue it is both counterproductive and dangerous.

*   **Asset Seizure vs. Traditional Taxation:** Investor and podcast host Jason Calacanis argues the wealth tax is not a standard income tax, but a cumbersome asset seizure. 
    *   It requires highly impractical valuations of illiquid assets, including private company shares, fine art, and personal property.
    *   The proposed valuation of founder shares with super-voting rights (valued at voting rights rather than asset value) has already accelerated the exit of major tech founders like Larry Page, Sergey Brin, Mark Zuckerberg, Travis Kalanick, and David Sacks from California.
*   **Tax Flight and Revenue Destruction:** Bradley Tusk (founder of Tusk Ventures and former Deputy Governor of Illinois) highlights the historical failure of jurisdictional tax increases. 
    *   Between 2012 and 2022, New York’s share of U.S. millionaires fell from 12.7% to 8.7% due to tax hikes and aggressive regulation. 
    *   This flight resulted in an estimated **$13 billion annual deficit** in lost tax revenue that could have funded critical social services like Medicaid and public housing.
*   **The "Slippery Slope" Threshold:** While the California measure targets billionaires, Tusk warns that the ballot's language allows the state legislature to expand the tax to any group consistent with the referendum's intent. This loophole could easily lower the asset threshold from $1 billion down to $1 million, effectively targeting average California homeowners.

## Political Demagoguery and Performative Legislation

The push for wealth taxes is increasingly driven by political opportunism on both sides of the aisle rather than sound fiscal policy.

*   **Exploiting Voter Anger:** Politicians on the extreme left and right secure votes and donations by stoking class resentment and promising "justice" or "revenge" against successful individuals.
*   **The Cost of Performative Politics:** Tusk points to New York Assemblyman Zohran Mamdani’s push for a Pied-à-Terre tax, which specifically targeted billionaire Ken Griffin. By making Griffin the face of the fight for political clout, the state risked losing Griffin's planned $6 billion office renovation in Manhattan, which would have created 15,000 jobs for New Yorkers.
*   **Safety Concerns:** Calacanis warns that the constant political vilification of successful people has created a dangerous environment, resulting in a dramatic rise in credible threats and the need for heavy security details among tech leaders.

## Realistic Tax and Labor Alternatives

Rather than implementing unconstitutional wealth taxes, the speakers propose practical, free-market adjustments to address economic inequality.

*   **Taxing Margin Loans:** A prominent loophole allows individuals with over $10 million in net worth to take out low-interest margin loans against their stock portfolios to fund their lifestyles without triggering capital gains taxes. Calacanis suggests implementing a tax on the origination of these margin loans.
*   **Gradual Minimum Wage Increases:** Raising the federal minimum wage (currently $7.25) by $1 per year over five years to reach $12 or more could stimulate the economy. Studies from the Nordics, Switzerland, and New Zealand show that higher minimum wages do not significantly impact the cost of consumer goods, but do turn lower-income citizens into active consumers who fuel economic growth.

## Structural and Political Reforms to Lower Costs

Addressing inequality requires reducing the cost of living and breaking the political gridlock that prevents moderate, compromise-driven solutions.

*   **Deregulating Key Sectors:** The three major areas driving middle-class anxiety—housing, education, and healthcare—are heavily monopolized and restricted by government regulations. 
    *   Deregulating university accreditations, streamlining housing permits (similar to Texas, Nevada, and Florida), and leveraging AI in healthcare could dramatically lower costs. For example, AI-driven diagnostics could reduce the price of a full-body scan from $3,500 to $30.
*   **Direct Wealth Transfers:** Tusk advocates for Universal Basic Income (UBI) and "Medicare for All" (with a private option) over bureaucratic tax-and-spend programs, noting that up to 40 cents of every tax dollar is lost to government overhead before reaching those in need.
*   **Political Voting Reform:** To bypass extreme primary voters (who currently dictate the political agenda due to low ~10% primary turnouts), Tusk's organization is advocating for secure **mobile voting** (`mobilevoting.org`). Increasing primary turnout to 30%–50% would force politicians to cater to the moderate majority and collaborate on practical legislation.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "It's a seizure of assets... Tell me everything in your house, Ed. Tell me every painting, tell me every car. Go find somebody to appraise my classic cars... and then we want 5% of those. It is an asset seizure of wealth I’ve already paid taxes on."  
> — **Jason Calacanis**

> "Every time that someone sent us a dollar in tax revenue, by the time that money reached the people in need, 30 to 40 cents on that dollar was gone... If California has less money to help the poor because wealthy people left, then you're not solving the problem of inequality."  
> — **Bradley Tusk**

> "The things that are breaking people are the cost of education, the cost of healthcare, and the cost of homes... We need to dramatically lower the cost of these three things by unleashing the same entrepreneurs who are currently being vilified."  
> — **Jason Calacanis**

> "There are reasonable, achievable solutions to almost every single problem we face... but the only way we can do that is to take the power away from the extremes who currently dictate and control the agenda, and give it back to the middle."  
> — **Bradley Tusk**

briefings.title: The Digital Fairness Act: Keynote Address by Isabelle Pérignon

people.name: Isabelle Pérignon
people.role: Director for Consumer Policy, European Commission

briefings.tldr: The upcoming Digital Fairness Act (DFA)—a flagship initiative of EU Commissioner Michael McGrath scheduled for adoption under the Irish EU Presidency—aims to modernize consumer protection by banning manipulative online practices like dark patterns and dynamic pricing.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
The upcoming Digital Fairness Act (DFA)—a flagship initiative of EU Commissioner Michael McGrath scheduled for adoption under the Irish EU Presidency—aims to modernize consumer protection by banning manipulative online practices like dark patterns and dynamic pricing. To ensure these rules are effectively enforced, the European Commission will simultaneously introduce a major reform of the Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Regulation to drastically accelerate investigations and enable direct penalties for cross-border violations.

---

## The Strategic Objectives of the Digital Fairness Act

*   **The 2030 Consumer Agenda:** This overarching policy framework operates on the principle that consumer protection and economic competitiveness are mutually reinforcing.
    *   **Economic Impact:** Consumer purchases represent approximately 51% of the European Union's GDP, making consumer choice a primary driver of the EU economy.
    *   **Market Integrity:** A healthy market must rely on consumers making choices based on price, quality, and product characteristics rather than manipulative digital tactics.
*   **Two Core Priorities:**
    *   **Vulnerable Consumers:** Special protections are being designed for minors, individuals with disabilities, and those who lack digital literacy.
    *   **Regulatory Simplification:** The Commission aims to simplify rules and reduce unnecessary administrative burdens for businesses by closing legal gaps rather than adding redundant regulatory layers.

## Tackling "Generation 2.0" Unfair Digital Practices

*   **Inadequacy of Legacy Laws:** Traditional frameworks, such as the 20-year-old Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, are struggling to address highly sophisticated, psychologically manipulative online architectures.
*   **Key Digital Targets of the DFA:**
    *   **Dark Patterns:** Interface designs that subtly steer consumer behavior beneath conscious awareness (e.g., making cookie acceptance a single click while hiding refusal options behind complex menus). The DFA aims to establish a list of specific prohibited dark patterns across the EU.
    *   **Dynamic Pricing:** Discriminatory practices where prices spike unexpectedly while consumers are waiting in virtual queues (e.g., ticket prices multiplying several-fold at checkout).
    *   **Subscription Traps:** Intentionally complex processes for canceling online contracts, and "free trial" models that automatically renew into costly, long-term subscriptions.
    *   **Minors and Addictive Design:** Features targeting youth, such as video game "loot boxes" and addictive user-experience designs that encourage excessive screen time and spending.

## Fostering a Level Playing Field for Businesses

*   **Preventing Single Market Fragmentation:** The European Commission wants to avoid a regulatory patchwork where EU member states enact differing national laws (such as recently observed national variations in influencer marketing laws). 
    *   An EU-level harmonized framework will provide much-needed legal certainty for businesses operating across all 27 member states.
*   **Promoting Quality Over Manipulation:** By cracking down on manipulative designs, the DFA seeks to reward compliant, high-quality businesses that compete transparently rather than those using deceptive tactics to capture market share.
*   **Regulatory Synergy:** The DFA is designed to act as a horizontal safety net, complementing existing major digital regulations like the Digital Services Act (DSA), the Digital Markets Act (DMA), and the AI Act without creating conflicting compliance burdens.

## Reforming Cross-Border Consumer Law Enforcement

*   **Current Bottlenecks:** Enforcement of EU consumer law currently takes an average of 18 months, and national authorities are frequently limited to securing voluntary commitments from non-compliant platforms.
*   **CPC Regulation Reform:** Alongside the DFA, the Commission will introduce a revised Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Regulation to strengthen the network of 30 national enforcement authorities (the 27 EU member states plus EEA partners).
*   **Enhanced Enforcement Powers:**
    *   **Stronger Deterrents:** Introducing faster investigative procedures and the power to impose substantial fines for cross-border violations.
    *   **Platform Suspension:** Granting authorities the power to suspend access to online platforms if they pose an imminent threat to consumers.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "Competitiveness and consumer policy are not in tension, but they are really mutually reinforcing. Consumers are the largest economic actors in the single market, with their purchases accounting for around 51% of the EU GDP."  
> — **Isabelle Pérignon**, Director for Consumer Policy, European Commission

> "Traders and sellers can know almost everything about consumers. They know their habits, they know their preferences, and even their purchasing power, while users are often left to interact only with interfaces, call centers, or chatbots... Asymmetries and unfairness in business-to-consumer commercial practices are therefore deeper than ever."  
> — **Isabelle Pérignon**, Director for Consumer Policy, European Commission

> "It's nice to have rules, but it's very important to be able to enforce them."  
> — **Isabelle Pérignon**, Director for Consumer Policy, European Commission

briefings.title: The future of U.S. foreign policy: Competing with China, U.S. reliability and a new warfare era

people.name: Linda Thomas-Greenfield
people.role: US Ambassador to the United Nations

briefings.tldr: To successfully compete with systemic rivals like China and navigate a new era of high-tech warfare, the United States must abandon unilateralism, rebuild its damaged international credibility, and foster agile, issue-specific global alliances.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
To successfully compete with systemic rivals like China and navigate a new era of high-tech warfare, the United States must abandon unilateralism, rebuild its damaged international credibility, and foster agile, issue-specific global alliances.

---

## China and the Power of Multilateral Alliances

*   **The Unilateral Deficit:** Former Secretary of State Antony Blinken warned that competing with China one-on-one is a losing proposition due to China's massive market, superior purchasing power parity, and manufacturing output, which is currently three times that of the U.S.
*   **The Power of Convergence:** Building allied coalitions is the primary strategic counterweight to China. 
    *   Aligning the U.S. with Europe, Japan, South Korea, India, Australia, and Canada shifts the coalition's economic weight from 20–25% of global GDP to 50–60%, making U.S.-led initiatives impossible for China to ignore.
*   **Declining Global Trust:** A poll of 130 countries revealed that China is currently viewed as a more credible international actor than the U.S. In Germany, a poll showed that 70% of respondents viewed the U.S. as an adversary.
*   **African Alignment:** Ambassador Linda Thomas-Greenfield noted that African nations are increasingly forced to choose sides, frequently favoring China because they currently view it as a more trustworthy and reliable partner than the U.S.

## Rebuilding U.S. Reliability and Diplomatic Credibility

*   **The Reliability Question:** Senator Andy Kim emphasized that the primary question foreign leaders ask about the U.S. is: *"Is America a reliable country?"* Rebuilding this baseline of consistency is a long-term challenge that will outlast any single presidential administration.
*   **Diplomatic Understaffing:** The U.S. is severely hamstringing its own foreign policy by failing to confirm diplomatic personnel. 
    *   The U.S. currently lacks Senate-confirmed ambassadors in over 100 countries, including 37 nations in Africa. This vacancy rate cripples the nation's ability to negotiate complex agreements or counter foreign influence.
*   **The Cost of Domestic Corruption:** Ambassador Thomas-Greenfield pointed out that reports of a past U.S. administration financially benefiting to the tune of $1.4 billion severely undercut American moral authority. This makes human rights and anti-corruption advocacy abroad appear hypocritical to foreign governments.

## Strategic Failures and Regional Fallout in the Middle East

*   **The Strategic Deficit in Iran:** Blinken characterized the U.S. conflict with Iran as a strategic failure. Despite any tactical successes, Iran is poised to retain its regime, its missile capabilities, vestiges of its nuclear program, and significant leverage over the Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes.
*   **Economic and Diplomatic Strain:**
    *   **Domestic Costs:** Senator Kim highlighted that the conflict has cost American consumers over $42 billion in increased gas and diesel prices.
    *   **Alienated Allies:** U.S. actions have alienated European allies (previously strained by disputes over NATO, Greenland, and Denmark) and frustrated Gulf partners who feel directly exposed to Iranian retaliation. Notably, Iran has fired more projectiles at the UAE than at Israel during this conflict.
*   **Diplomatic Off-Ramps:** Resolving the standoff will require highly skilled negotiation and compromise. Potential terms include down-blending Iran's highly enriched uranium, a temporary enrichment moratorium, and a Strait of Hormuz tolling system to fund regional reconstruction.

## The War in Ukraine and the Future of Warfare

*   **Resilience on the Battlefield:** Despite declining U.S. funding, Ukraine is holding its military and economic lines with European aid. Meanwhile, Russia’s war economy is beginning to cannibalize itself as defense spending fails to generate productive domestic infrastructure.
*   **Weapons of Mass Production:** Senator Kim warned that modern warfare has shifted from "weapons of mass destruction" to "weapons of mass production." The battlefield is now defined by the rapid, high-volume manufacturing of drones, AI tools (such as Mithos), and ballistic missiles.
*   **Rapid Tech Acceleration:** The pace of global change is unprecedented. Blinken noted that while the telephone took 75 years to reach 50 million users, Instagram took 4 years, and ChatGPT reached the milestone in just 4 months.
*   **Variable Geometry:** Future global governance will move away from rigid autocracy-versus-democracy blocs. Instead, the U.S. must lead via "variable geometry"—agile, issue-specific coalitions of countries, companies, and civil actors collaborating on targeted problems like climate change, AI governance, and food security.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "If we're competing with China one-on-one, that's a game that we may lose... But when we're aligned with Europe, with Japan, with Korea, with India, with Australia, with Canada, we go from about 20, 25% of world GDP to 50 or 60%, a lot harder for China to ignore."
> — *Antony Blinken, Former Secretary of State*

> "It makes us look like hypocrites. It is a very hard conversation to have with a foreign government where you know you're talking to them about corruption in their country and they're going to talk back to you about what's happening in your country."
> — *Linda Thomas-Greenfield, Ambassador*

> "We are finding ourselves in a place where we are trying to navigate these weapons of mass production—this idea of what it is when you're able to produce such quantity, with drones, ballistic missiles... That is the future."
> — *Sen. Andy Kim*

> "There's a lot of understandable nostalgia for the past... But the reality is you can't put the genie back in the bottle. You've got to shape a new bottle, and that's what these conversations have to all be about."
> — *Antony Blinken, Former Secretary of State*

briefings.title: What Trump and Xi Didn't Settle in Beijing, With Nicholas Burns | The President’s Inbox
briefings.tldr: While the recent Trump-Xi summit in Beijing established a temporary, detente-like cooling of tensions and yielded modest agricultural and aviation deals, it highlighted deep strategic divides over Iran, technology competition, and a highly controversial potential shift in US Taiwan policy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
While the recent Trump-Xi summit in Beijing established a temporary, detente-like cooling of tensions and yielded modest agricultural and aviation deals, it highlighted deep strategic divides over Iran, technology competition, and a highly controversial potential shift in US Taiwan policy.

---

## Summit Atmosphere, Communication, and Key Economic Outcomes

*   **A "Detente-Like" Climate:** Former US Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns characterized the summit as highly consequential, noting a visible, visceral cooling of bilateral tensions that have persisted for the last seven to eight years.
*   **The Absence of a Joint Communique:** Consistent with meetings during the Biden administration, no joint written communique was produced. 
    *   **Profound Differences:** The core policy disagreements between Washington and Beijing remain too severe to negotiate a mutually agreed-upon text. Instead, both sides issued separate, mismatched statements highlighting their respective priorities.
*   **Key Commercial Agreements:** 
    *   **Agricultural Purchases:** China committed to purchasing at least $17 billion of US agricultural products for the remainder of the calendar year, and $25 billion annually for the following three years. 
    *   **Aviation Sales:** China agreed to purchase 200 Boeing aircraft. While smaller than some analysts anticipated, Burns viewed this as a positive step forward for a vital commercial sector.
    *   **Tariff and Supply Chain Truce:** No official tariff truce was announced. This was likely delayed as the US recalibrates its tariff structures in response to recent Supreme Court decisions challenging executive authority.

---

## Geopolitical Friction: Iran and the Middle East

*   **Shared High-Level Rhetoric:** China publicly reiterated its long-standing positions that Iran should not become a nuclear power and that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open to free navigation.
*   **Limits of Chinese Leverage:** Burns expressed skepticism that China would actively pressure Tehran into a ceasefire, particularly if the US resumes threats of military force against Iran.
*   **The Authoritarian Axis:** China’s closest partners remain Russia, North Korea, and Iran—a coalition actively working together to support Russia's war in Ukraine. 
*   **Strategic Inaction:** China has deliberately avoided taking a proactive role in brokering Middle East peace.
    *   **Distracting the US:** Beijing is content to watch the US remain bogged down in Middle East conflicts, which has forced Washington to divert carrier battle groups and air defense assets away from the Indo-Pacific theater.

---

## The Taiwan Question and Potential US Policy Shifts

*   **Xi's Early Warnings:** The Chinese delegation took the unusual step of leaking President Xi Jinping's opening private statement mid-morning, firing a warning shot that crossing China's "red lines" on Taiwan could lead to direct conflict.
*   **Trump's Air Force One Comments:** On his return flight, President Trump equivocated on whether the US would maintain its 50-year-old "One China" policy, hinting that defense arms sales to Taiwan could be used as a bargaining chip.
*   **Severe Repercussions of a Policy U-Turn:** Burns warned that weakening support for Taiwan would be a historic strategic blunder.
    *   **Legal Obligations:** Defense arms sales to Taiwan are legally mandated by the US Taiwan Relations Act of 1979.
    *   **Economic Vitality:** Taiwan’s advanced semiconductor industry (TSMC) is critical to the global technology supply chain.
    *   **Damage to Alliances:** Abandoning Taiwan would severely erode US credibility with key Indo-Pacific allies (Japan, the Philippines, South Korea, and Australia) and NATO partners, who rely on the reliability of US defense commitments.

---

## Technology Competition and Bilateral AI Regulation

*   **The Core Global Battleground:** Technology has become the central front in the US-China relationship. Leadership in artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and quantum computing will determine which nation is the dominant global power by the 2030s and 2040s.
*   **The "Mythos" AI Wake-Up Call:** Anthropic’s advanced "Mythos" model has raised alarm bells. The potential for cyber-terrorists, bio-terrorists, or criminal syndicates to weaponize advanced AI has forced both the US and China to seek bilateral guardrails.
*   **Agreement to Negotiate:** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and President Trump confirmed that the US and China have agreed to launch formal security talks regarding AI risk mitigation.
*   **Building on Past Precedent:** This follows an agreement brokered at the end of the Biden administration in Lima, Peru, where both countries publicly declared that human beings—not AI systems—must remain in control of nuclear weapons.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "One thing I learned in China, Jim, flattery will get you nowhere. It's all about the bottom line." 
> — Nicholas Burns

> "If President Trump does make this U-turn, refuse to provide the arms that the Taiwanese have asked for... I think this could be the most significant mistake along with the Iran war of President Trump's second term of office." 
> — Nicholas Burns

> "You know the old adage, 'Why interrupt, don't interrupt your enemy while your enemy's making a big mistake.' Napoleon's advice... and the Chinese subscribe to it, so it hasn't surprised me that they haven't tried to be a dealmaker [in the Middle East]." 
> — Nicholas Burns
